question: Of blood groups O, A and AB, which waits longest on average for a kidney from a deceased donor?
options: Group AB, the rarest of the three
Group O, the commonest of the three
answer: Group O. An O kidney is compatible with patients of every group, but an O patient can accept only an O kidney. Left alone, other groups drain the O supply, so allocation schemes now reserve O kidneys mostly for O patients. AB patients can take any group and wait least.
move: Whoever can give to everyone may be the one left waiting.
ask: Who in my life can help everyone and ends up waiting themselves?
trap: Picking AB, reasoning that the rarest group is hardest to match.
source: NHS Blood and Transplant, kidney transplantation report
reference: NHS Blood and Transplant, Annual Report on Kidney Transplantation 2022/23, 2023
